solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Big gun, that thing in bronze (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the short word inside the longer one, as a thing sits in a casing

annotation.surface: An artillery piece described as cast in bronze.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Big gun' reads as a cannon, but it is a person of power.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a big gun is an important, powerful figure, and so is a giant of industry or politics.

entries.clue: I doubt I can go wrong touring street (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is what an agnostic says, standing for the person who says it.

indicatorNotes.wrong: the letters of I CAN GO go wrong, landing in the wrong order
indicatorNotes.touring: to tour is to travel round, so the rearranged letters go round ST

annotation.surface: A nervous walker fretting about getting lost on the way round a street.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I doubt' is the doubter's own creed in two words, so the definition is a quotation rather than a synonym. The clue has two separate I's: one opens the definition, the other starts the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by quotation: someone who holds that God's existence cannot be known says 'I doubt'.

entries.clue: Parasite in swab? (6)

blocks.note: someone who lives off other people's generosity
as a verb: to mop or wipe clean with an absorbent pad

annotation.surface: A microbe found on a medical swab.
annotation.walkthrough: SPONGE works both ways: a sponger cadges off others, and you sponge a wound clean. The surface wants a lab bug on a cotton bud.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: a person who scrounges, and the act of wiping with an absorbent pad.

entries.clue: Support for piano (4)

annotation.surface: A stand or leg to hold up a piano.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a piano stand; 'for' is the Latin-derived PRO and 'piano' the musical marking P.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prop is anything that holds something else up, a beam or a stake.

entries.clue: Suit that gentleman crafts (6)

annotation.surface: A tailor at work: the suit that a gentleman makes.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like tailoring, but it is a suit of playing cards.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: one of the four suits in a pack of cards, alongside clubs, diamonds and spades.

entries.clue: High-pitched sound, call of small animal, runt (9)

blocks.note: a pip is a short high tone, as in the radio time signal

annotation.surface: A list of the feeble noises a runt of the litter makes.
annotation.walkthrough: The pips are the short beeps of the BBC time signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a runt is the smallest and weakest, and the answer is a small, insignificant person.

entries.clue: Country artiste disappointing, by the sound of it? (9)

indicatorNotes.by the sound of it: tells you to judge by how the words sound when said, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: a performer who is not good

annotation.surface: A critic panning a country-music performer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country artiste' reads as a country singer, but 'Country' is the definition, split off from 'artiste'. In a non-rhotic British accent SINGER POOR sounds like the city-state.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a city-state country at the tip of the Malay peninsula.

entries.clue: Demonic soul resided to the west (5)

indicatorNotes.to the west: in an across clue, west is leftward, so the word runs backwards

annotation.surface: An evil spirit that once dwelt out west.
annotation.walkthrough: LIVED and its reverse are a famous crossword pair.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the chief evil spirit, and any lesser demon, is called by this name.

entries.clue: Very cold, nipper grabbing coat, finally (6)

indicatorNotes.grabbing: to grab is to seize and hold, so the outer word holds the letter within it
indicatorNotes.finally: 'finally' points to the end of the word, its last letter

annotation.surface: A freezing child snatching a coat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nipper' looks like a child, but here it is one who nips, a BITER.
annotation.definitionFit: Describes cold that bites, as in a raw wind, so it means very cold rather than merely chilly.

entries.clue: Desert area half covered by orbiter (6)

indicatorNotes.half: 'half' asks for half the word's letters, here the front two of four
indicatorNotes.covered by: to be covered by something is to sit under and inside it, so MOON wraps round

annotation.surface: A satellite passing over half of a desert region.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun for sand, but it is the verb, to abandon.
annotation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to leave someone stranded, typically on an island, is to desert them.

entries.clue: Flowering plant Victorian grew (8)

blocks.note: prim, prudish, as Victorian values were

annotation.surface: A plant that a Victorian gardener raised.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' is used as an adjective meaning strait-laced.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a pale yellow spring flower of woods and hedgerows.

entries.clue: Irregular stripe runs through meat (6)

indicatorNotes.through: something that runs through a thing passes into its middle

annotation.surface: A marbled vein of fat running through a steak.
annotation.walkthrough: R for runs comes from cricket scorecards.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long, uneven line of colour, like a streak of lightning.

entries.clue: Furry pet in pool? (5)

blocks.note: a child's word for a cat
a shared fund that everyone puts money into, as in a card game

annotation.surface: A cat that has fallen into a swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: KITTY is both a cat and a pot of money. 'Pool' is not water but pooled cash.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a pet name for a cat, and a joint fund into which players or flatmates pay.

entries.clue: Wipe face on towel with difficulty (6)

indicatorNotes.face: the face of a word is its front, the first letter

annotation.surface: Someone struggling to dry their face with a towel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wipe' is the noun, a disposable cloth, not the verb the surface suggests.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: a paper tissue is a disposable wipe for the face or nose.

entries.clue: Huge crowd, and thus so unruly (9)

indicatorNotes.unruly: the letters are rowdy and will not stay in order

annotation.surface: A vast crowd that is therefore hard to control.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' looks like a joining word, but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An indefinite large number standing for a multitude, as in 'they turned up in their ...'.

entries.clue: Elegant, such iconic jackets (4)

indicatorNotes.jackets: as a verb: the two words wrap around the answer like a jacket

blocks.note: suCH ICtonic: the letters run across the word gap

annotation.surface: Praise for a fashion line's iconic, elegant jackets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Jackets' looks like the clothing in a fashion review, but it is a verb: the phrase encloses the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym borrowed from French: stylish, fashionable, elegant.

entries.clue: Future husband not in fluster (5)

indicatorNotes.not in: H is not to be in the word, so it comes out

annotation.surface: A bride-to-be's fiancé who is not at all nervous.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Future husband' reads as a fiancé; 'Future' alone is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: something to come, as in 'a future date' or 'a later date'.

entries.clue: Old story, member reaching last page? (6)

blocks.note: a leg is a limb, or member
surface joinery: the limb reaches the end, so LEG runs straight on into END
the last page of a book is its end

annotation.surface: A club member reaching the final page of an ancient tale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Member' looks like a person in a club, but it is a limb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a traditional tale handed down from long ago, like those of King Arthur.

entries.clue: Objective opinion initially welcomed by lass (4)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so take the first letter
indicatorNotes.welcomed by: to be welcomed by someone is to be taken into their arms, so GAL takes the O inside

annotation.surface: A girl receptive to a neutral view.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Objective' looks like an adjective, unbiased, which fits 'opinion'; it is the noun, an aim.
annotation.definitionFit: Noun sense: an objective is an aim you work towards, a synonym of target.

entries.clue: Demonic soul with high forms (8)

indicatorNotes.forms: as a verb: the letters are formed into a new word

annotation.surface: An evil spirit taking shapes up high.
annotation.walkthrough: 8 across used 'Demonic soul' as its whole definition; here 'soul' is anagram fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Like a ghoul, a grave-robbing demon of folklore, so fiendish and morbid.

entries.clue: Smell bad minibeast in moonshine (6)

blocks.note: to hum is British slang for to stink
a bug is a small creature

annotation.surface: An insect smelling foul after drowning in illicit liquor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moonshine' looks like bootleg spirit, but it also means nonsense.
annotation.definitionFit: Both mean nonsense or empty talk, as in Scrooge's 'Bah!' dismissal of Christmas.

entries.clue: Weaver of dream in bed (6)

blocks.note: Nick, the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
the ground under a river or the sea, as in a river bed

annotation.surface: Someone spinning a dream while lying in bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dream' is Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, whose weaver Nick BOTTOM is given an ass's head. A river bed is its bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a Shakespearean character's name, and the floor of a river or sea.

entries.clue: Chicken and mustard (6)

annotation.surface: A menu line: chicken served with mustard.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a dish; both words are adjectives. YELLOW means cowardly, and mustard is its shade.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for cowardly, like 'chicken', and the colour named after the condiment.

entries.clue: Corporate colours – as producer of bile? (6)

blocks.note: the colour scheme on a company's vans, planes or uniforms
like the organ that makes bile, with -Y added as in 'fishy'

annotation.surface: Wondering whether a company's colours are as sickly as bile.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is whimsical: read LIVERY as 'liver-y', like a liver, and the question mark admits the stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a firm's distinctive colours, and a made-up adjective for resembling the bile-producing organ.

entries.clue: Swift finding power in swoop (5)

indicatorNotes.finding: joins definition to wordplay: the answer is found by the step that follows
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' places the letter inside the word

blocks.note: a swoop is a sudden raid

annotation.surface: A swift, the bird, putting power into its dive.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like the bird that swoops, but it is the adjective, fast.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean moving or happening at great speed.

entries.clue: Bolt perhaps quicker, men caught, but not leader! (8)

indicatorNotes.caught: to be caught is to be trapped inside, so FASTER holds the letters
indicatorNotes.not leader: 'leader' is the first letter, and 'not' removes it

annotation.surface: Usain Bolt, perhaps, going faster than the other runners.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' tempts you towards the sprinter Usain Bolt, which 'quicker' encourages; here it is a door bolt.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a door bolt is one kind of catch or clasp, and 'perhaps' flags the example.

entries.clue: Food originally consumed by vermin, considerable amount (4)

indicatorNotes.originally: 'originally' means at the origin, the first letter
indicatorNotes.consumed by: what is consumed ends up inside the eater, so RAT takes in F

annotation.surface: Rats eating a large quantity of stored food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Food' looks like what the vermin eat, but only its first letter is eaten.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal sense: a large collection of things, as in 'a whole ... of new measures'.

entries.clue: Coarse cloth darling reversed (6)

annotation.surface: A rough fabric beloved but turned inside out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Coarse cloth' reads as sacking, but 'Coarse' alone is the definition. LUV is the chatty British spelling of love, used to anyone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacking refinement, crude in manners or taste.

entries.clue: One in mixer turned over for so long (5)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' puts the letter inside the word
indicatorNotes.turned over: something turned over is upside down, and in a word that means it runs backwards

annotation.surface: Someone at a party capsizing their drink for good.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mixer' is a drink added to spirits, not a party or a kitchen gadget.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed Spanish farewell, used in English as a jokey goodbye.

entries.clue: Previous idea so far failing (9)

indicatorNotes.failing: something failing falls apart, so the letters collapse into a new order

annotation.surface: An earlier plan that has not worked out so far.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a project update; the three words are just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Legal-style synonym: mentioned earlier in the same document.
